summary: xAI announced that Grok Bot, its agentic AI teammate product, is now included at no extra cost with SuperGrok, Cursor Pro, and Cursor Teams subscription plans, with usage tracked separately from existing plan quotas.

mechanisms.reason: The announcement describes autonomous, parallel, always-on agents handling delegated tasks across apps in place of manual seat-based work, expanded to a wider user base.
mechanisms.quote: They're digital teammates you can message, run in parallel, and trust to finish work in the tools you already use.

practices.reason: Teams already on SuperGrok or Cursor Pro/Teams plans now have Grok Bot access with separate usage quotas, which changes what is available in their existing stack and worth evaluating.
practices.quote: Grok Bot comes with its own usage, separate from your Grok and Cursor plans, so anything you hand off to a Bot won't count against your existing usage.

practices.reason: The multi-agent group-chat pattern for passing work between bots is described as a product feature without a stated gain or implementation detail an engineering team could replicate.
practices.quote: Many Bots at once. Stand up a researcher, writer, and chief of staff. Put them in a group chat so they pass work between themselves, and you're not in the middle.
